slot.brief: Series LCR with given R, L, C and source frequency; compute the impedance (and optionally power factor) by direct formula.

stem: A series LCR circuit has resistance $12\ \Omega$, inductance $0.10$ H and capacitance $2.0\times10^{-3}$ F. If its angular frequency is $100$ rad s$^{-1}$, what is its impedance?
working:
$X_L=\omega L=10\ \Omega$, $X_C=\dfrac{1}{\omega C}=5\ \Omega$\n$Z=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}$\n$Z=\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=13\ \Omega$

Independent check: X_L=[? no need. Compute X_L=100(0.10)=10 Ω; X_C=1/(100·0.002)=5 Ω. Hence Z=√(12²+(10−5)²)=13 Ω.
solution:
For a series LCR circuit, $Z=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}$, where $X_L=\omega L=10\,\Omega$ and $X_C=\dfrac{1}{\omega C}=5\,\Omega$.
$$Z=\sqrt{12^2+(10-5)^2}=13\,\Omega$$
